body.target_estimand: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) is the structural target; the established fixed-\(A\) result is \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)\subseteq\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)\), while equality with a fixed local-rule closure is conditional on faithful realization and an observable unknown-\(A\) extension theorem.
body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\iff\mu_\eta(e)=m\text{ for every }\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O);\quad \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\text{ otherwise}\)

sampling_model.design: Oracle graphical analysis from the observational MAG signature and \(K\) pooled intervention-regime MAG signatures generated by one common basal selected DAG. The canonical SI-PAG is the structural target; the established result is a partial fixed-\(A\) bracket and a conditional completeness reduction.
sampling_model.units: The primitive object is a fully specified member \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\). At \(K=0\), its only oracle law is \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\); at \(K\ge 1\), each comparison additionally uses \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Regime membership is observed, while every direct soft-intervention target set \(T_k(\eta)\) is latent and may differ from the indicator-neighbor set \(Z_k\).
sampling_model.overlap: The common pre-treatment selection event has positive probability, so every selected oracle law is well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not applicable to the proved oracle results. The core supplies no finite-sample conditional-independence or invariance tests, separation margin, or simultaneous confidence theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 proves CDIS soundness, while p. 8, lines 652--661, states that completeness is uncertain.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: This note proves a fixed-selection-ancestry graphical mark bracket and restates full local completeness as a conditional future implication; it does not close Dai et al.'s completeness gap.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sections 3--4 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for one observational PAG, with Theorem 2 giving a representative-MAG construction.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The proposed synchronized handle is informed by Zhang's rules, but no multi-regime common-basal extension theorem is proved.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Markov equivalence of maximal ancestral graphs is characterized by adjacencies and colliders with order.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Those invariants motivate signature preservation; the present proved result is only a graphical replacement and fixed-A endpoint bracket.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The public abstract describes a known-target enumeration-based completion; official theorem text was inaccessible.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: This note excludes global enumeration as the headline method and does not yet supply a complete local alternative for unknown targets and selection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper presents a polynomial-delay MAG listing method.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Only a conditional polynomial bound for saturation of a supplied fixed rule list is retained; no listing or complete calculus is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper gives a complete characterization under soft interventions with unknown targets and no selection bias.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present selected common-basal setting remains only partially characterized, so there is no matched completeness claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The public record describes a sound and complete F-FCI algorithm for latent confounding with post-treatment selection.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The timing and model class differ, and this note makes no competing completeness claim in its pre-treatment selected class.

body.tldr: Selection before perturbation couples all regime MAGs through one basal selected DAG. This round proves a graphical replacement theorem, a nonempty fixed-\(A(\eta)\) faithful-model mark bracket with exact singleton cases, and two signature-preserving graphical specifications for the two-mark case. It also proves that simultaneous faithfulness reduces to atomic determinant nontriviality and that faithful realization plus a finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension theorem would imply equality of rule closure with the canonical SI-PAG and polynomial saturation. Faithful promotion and the finite extension calculus remain open, so no complete SI-PAG algorithm or opposing faithful-witness theorem is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. prove CDIS soundness and leave completeness uncertain; their fixed-model endpoint semantics do not supply opposing common-basal faithful representatives. Zhang proves completeness for one observational PAG, not synchronized intervention regimes. Known-target enumeration results do not provide the required unknown-target, pre-treatment-selection local extension. The remaining gaps here are now isolated as atomic faithful realization and finite observable unknown-\(A\) extension.
project_justification.niche: The achieved contribution is a technical partial characterization for Dai et al.'s class: an observable selectedness certificate, a fixed-selection-ancestry graphical endpoint bracket, signature-preserving replacement specifications, and a conditional reduction to canonical completeness. This is not positioned as a field-level completeness result.
project_justification.fill: The note separates three layers. It proves graphical preservation and the fixed-\(A(\eta)\) mark-set inclusion, including exact singleton identifications; it proves the polynomial exceptional-set reduction for joint faithfulness; and it proves the endpointwise conditional implication from faithful realization and an observable unknown-\(A\) extension property to the canonical SI-PAG, with conditional polynomial saturation. It leaves both antecedents explicit and does not use global basal-DAG enumeration as a substitute.

body.related_work: Dai et al.'s Lemmas 4--6 characterize intervention-created adjacencies, indicator neighborhoods, and endpoint semantics in the pre-treatment-selection twin class; their Theorem 3 establishes CDIS soundness, and their discussion leaves completeness uncertain. Zhang's Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for a single observational PAG, but do not synchronize several pooled intervention projections through one basal selected DAG. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes supply single-MAG equivalence invariants that motivate signature preservation, not common-basal realizability. The public Zhou--Kocaoglu abstract describes known-target completion by compatible-MAG enumeration and additional local tightening rules; this note neither imports a formula-level theorem from that inaccessible source nor claims a complete local replacement. Wang, Du, and Zhou inform only the conditional computational accounting. Jaber et al. address unknown-target interventions without selection, while Luo et al. address a distinct post-treatment-selection setting. Relative to all of these comparators, the present achievement is a fixed-\(A\) graphical bracket and conditional reduction, not completeness.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The replacement construction names a graphical specification, not a probability model. Signature preservation does not prove that its equality-constrained shared-response-function realization fiber contains a jointly faithful member. The exact residual statistical task is atomic determinant nontriviality for every m-connected query. Even if that task is solved, observable certificates identify only a subset of every compatible ancestral selected set; a finite local rule system must still synchronize unknown selectedness and one exterior basal completion across all regimes. The current results do not establish simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs, because no finite-sample testing assumptions, separation margin, or error-control theorem is present in the frozen core.
body.honest_scope: Proved content consists of the graphical replacement preservation lemma already in the core; the conditional characterization of every fully specified replacement-fiber member; the fixed-\(A(\eta)\) inclusion \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A\subseteq\mathcal G_A\), with exact tail-only and arrow-only cases; empty-graph and simple-path signature-preserving graphical specifications in the two-mark case; the finite algebraic exceptional-set reduction; and the conditional endpointwise completeness and polynomial-saturation implications. Nonemptiness of arbitrary replacement realization fibers, opposing faithful witnesses in the two-mark case, a fixed observable unknown-\(A\) rule list, unconditional equality with the canonical SI-PAG, and simultaneous finite-sample confidence guarantees remain open. The scope is finite-alphabet, causally sufficient, childless pre-treatment selection with pooled binary-indicator regime laws; latent common causes, post-treatment selection, regime-specific selection mechanisms, and a global basal-DAG enumerator as headline calculus are excluded. The achieved positioning is therefore a rigorous technical foundation and partial characterization, explicitly below a field-level completeness contribution.
